The plan is safe and fits Nessa. It keeps her Monday, Wednesday and Saturday walk-run routine and leaves dog walks free on the other days. Every session is easy and can be run as written: 8×(2 min run / 1 min walk) on Monday and Wednesday, then 9 rounds on Saturday. After one missed week with no illness or pain, coming back at a similar level is reasonable. It's a small step up at most, not a rushed return. Nothing in the week calls for a referral or extra rest.

It loses a point for a few things:
- The opening misreads her note. She wrote "excited for next week" this week, but the draft treats it as a mood that came before the zero.
- It doesn't ask why she missed the week.
- It says the plan repeats "what already worked", which the card doesn't support.
- From what is shown, it never ties the week to the 15 November 5K or her goal of running it without walking. That is likely only a few weeks away.

A solid, runnable restart, but it could fit this week more closely.

Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3, 2.8, 7 km
This week: 0 km over 0 runs. Missed 3 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "All good."
Feeling: "Feeling great, excited for next week."

Tells Nessa: You went from "excited for next week" to zero runs, so this week is a careful restart at what already worked. …
Reading the week. The plan asked for three walk-run sessions on Mon, Wed and Sat and none of them happened, which is the main thing to understand.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 24 min walk-run, 8 rounds of 2 min easy run and 1 min walk, flat route. Eases…
Tue: rest. Full recovery day, dog walk is fine.
Wed: easy, 24 min walk-run, 8 rounds of 2 min easy run and 1 min walk, same effort as…
Thu: rest. Keep it to walking only so Saturday has legs under it.
Fri: rest. Protects the slightly longer Saturday session.
Sat: easy, 27 min walk-run, 9 rounds of 2 min easy run and 1 min walk, flat route. One…
Sun: rest. Dog walk is welcome, no running.
